Phases 0 · 1 · 2 · 4 — running

Visage

A client answers a questionnaire, uploads documents through an encrypted pipeline, and an attorney opens a filled Form I-485 generated from those answers. These are screenshots of it actually running, not mockups.

157 tests passing Form I-485, edition 01/20/25 54 fields filled from a questionnaire Phase 3 extraction not built

The client's side

Sign in with a firm code, because email is unique per firm — the same person can be a client of two different firms and hold an account at each.

localhost:3000/login

Every failure — unknown firm, unknown email, wrong password — returns one identical message. Distinguishing them would hand an attacker a membership oracle.

The questionnaire

Branching, resumable, and saved on every answer. Someone may be doing this on a phone across several sittings, and losing a page of work to a dropped connection is how people abandon the process.

localhost:3000/portal/intake

Section progress counts only visible questions, so answering "yes" to "have you used other names?" reveals a follow-up and the denominator goes up.

localhost:3000/portal/intake?section=eligibility

The 63 Part 9 eligibility questions are extracted verbatim from the official I-485, not retyped. The applicant signs under penalty of perjury, so the phrasing is legally load-bearing. Scroll the frame to see the run of them.

The checklist builds itself

localhost:3000/portal

Every item here was derived from an answer. Married → marriage certificate. Entered on F-1 → Form I-20. Arrested → certified court disposition, worded to cover the dismissed and expunged cases applicants assume don't count.

The medical exam has no upload control, deliberately. Form I-693 arrives from the civil surgeon in a sealed envelope, and opening it to scan it voids the exam. That is a schema column (uploadable), not a UI convention, so no future screen can get it wrong.

The attorney's side

localhost:3000/console

Sorted by what needs a human, not by recency. A case with documents waiting outranks one merely touched most recently — an inbox sorted by time makes the attorney do the triage the software should have done.

localhost:3000/console/case/…

The canonical profile, the uploaded document with its hash and scan status, and the audit trail. Every row in Recent activity is a real append-only audit record.

The document pipeline

upload→quarantine→ scan→sanitise→encrypt→ main bucket

The order is the point. Presigned direct-to-bucket uploads are the usual pattern and are wrong here — they put unscanned attacker-controlled bytes in the bucket we serve from. Nothing is ever served out of quarantine, and the quarantine object is deleted whether ingestion succeeds or fails.

StepWhat it doesWhy
detectReads magic bytes The declared MIME is attacker-controlled. Unrecognised types are rejected, never stored with a guessed content type.
scanStructural checks + EICAR Flags /JavaScript, /Launch, /OpenAction in a PDF an attorney will open.
sanitiseqpdf rewrite / sharp re-encode Drops active content from PDFs and EXIF from images — passport photos routinely carry the GPS coordinates of someone's home.
encryptPer-document key, wrapped per firm A leaked bucket yields ciphertext. Destroying a firm's key crypto-shreds their documents.

The bundled scanner is not antivirus, and says so. It catches active content and type confusion so the pipeline is exercised in CI without a ClamAV daemon. Production sets SCANNER=clamav. Calling it antivirus would be the dangerous kind of convenient.

PDFs are rewritten rather than rasterised. Rasterising is the more obvious way to neutralise a PDF, but it destroys the text layer that Phase 3's extraction will need.

Three things only the real form tells you

Caught by a test

The A-Number repeats on all 24 pages — and the names aren't derivable

Filling only the first leaves 23 pages looking blank to a reviewing officer. I generated the field names by pattern — and the subform indices skip 19, so #subform[i].AlienNumber[i] is right for the first nineteen pages and wrong for the last five. 19 of 24 filled. The mapping now reads the list from the committed field dump.

Reported, not hidden

Part 14 has exactly four continuation slots

Each needs a page, part, and item number — the bookkeeping human preparers fumble. The demo applicant generates five continuations, so the generator reports overflowDropped: 1 rather than silently truncating. Additional sheets are not built yet, and it says so instead of pretending.

Free integrity check

The barcodes state the edition

Every page carries a PDF417 barcode reading I-485|01/20/25|<page> — form code, edition, page. They encode no applicant data, so filling never invalidates them. The generator asserts the embedded edition matches the mapping and refuses to fill otherwise: USCIS rejects superseded editions, so a beautifully filled wrong-edition form is worse than an error.

Run it yourself

The session that built this runs in an ephemeral container, so there is no URL that outlives it. This is the honest alternative: four commands to the same screens.

# needs Docker and Node 20+
git clone <repo> && cd visage
docker compose up -d          # Postgres 16
cp .env.example .env && npm install

npm run db:setup              # roles, schema, RLS — verifies itself
npm run db:seed               # a firm, an attorney, a client
npm run demo                  # the applicant in these screenshots
npm run dev                   # http://localhost:3000

Sign in with firm code alpha, as client@alpha.test or attorney@alpha.test, password visage-dev-password. The seed refuses to run when NODE_ENV=production.

Deploying this for real needs a Postgres host, an S3-compatible bucket, and a KMS key — plus a decision about where. Vercel and Neon would take about an hour, but it needs your accounts, and I'd rather you make that call than have me pick.

What isn't built

  • Phase 3, document extraction. Uploads are stored and served but not yet read. docType is UNCLASSIFIED and the profile comes entirely from the questionnaire — which is why the case view labels every row "Questionnaire".
  • Phases 5–7. The overlay PDF editor and attorney sign-off, secure chat and page-anchored markup, and final package assembly.
  • Field coverage. The mapping covers the identity and status fields end to end. Parts 8 and 9 are 295 more fields, and mapping them is mechanical work against the committed dump rather than new architecture.
  • Print fidelity. Part 14 is a rich-text field, so appearance streams are delegated to the viewer via NeedAppearances. Acrobat honours it; some printers render such fields blank. Since this ends in a printed package, that needs a rendered-image check before anyone files.

Screenshots captured from the running application on 26 August 2026. The Form I-485 shown is a draft: nothing in Visage reaches a filable state without a licensed attorney approving it.
